plan_title: Oxy West Seminole San Andres Unit Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The West Seminole San Andres Unit boundary plus a half-mile buffer; the reservoir model forecast shows CO2 staying inside the unit (p15-16).
mma_definition: Same as the AMA: the unit boundary plus a half-mile buffer (p16).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Wellbores and surface equipment are treated as the only meaningful pathways; faults (a Devonian fault about a mile below the zone), seismicity, previous operations, lateral migration, drilling and diffuse seal leakage are rated low or no risk (p8, p17-21).
baseline_summary: No pre-injection environmental baseline. Existing automated operational data (injection set points, production forecasts, inspection work orders, H2S alarms) are used to flag excursions from expected performance (p28-29).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report filed by March 31 with other GHG reports, with the mass balance and leakage estimates; equipment leaks reported under Subpart W; records kept at least three years; the discontinuation request is to include two to three or more years of post-injection data. No commitment to publish data or report to the state UIC program (p27-28, p34, p37).

rows.detail: Custody transfer meter on CO2 received from the Permian Basin pipeline and an operations meter at the recompression facility outlet; composition sampled at least quarterly.
rows.location: Custody transfer point and recompression facility outlet
rows.evidence_quote: This meter measures flow rate continually.

rows.detail: Injection pressure monitored continually against pattern plans programmed into remotely operated WAG satellites; automatic flags on deviations and automatic shutoff on overpressure; SCADA monitors wellhead pressure.
rows.location: Each injection well and WAG satellite
rows.trigger_or_response: Pressure or rate outside set points: automatic flag, field investigation, work order; WAG skids shut off if pressure exceeds programmed levels.
rows.evidence_quote: Pressure in injection wells is monitored on a continual basis.

rows.detail: Annular pressure in wellheads monitored to detect tubing and casing leaks.
rows.trigger_or_response: Anomaly: inspect and repair; if extensive, well shut in, work order, leak quantified.
rows.evidence_quote: monitoring of the annular pressure in wellheads

rows.detail: MITs on injectors listed in the response plan as the check for tubing and casing leaks; no testing interval or rule citation given.
rows.trigger_or_response: Tubing or casing leak: wellbore shut in, workover crews respond within days.
rows.evidence_quote: Monitor changes in tubing and annulus pressure; MIT for injectors

rows.detail: Each producer tested about once every two months through satellite test stations (8-12 hours); produced gas sampled at least quarterly for CO2; results compared with forecast.
rows.location: Each production well; satellite test stations; recompression facility inlet
rows.trigger_or_response: Significant deviation from forecast: well management personnel investigate; work order if unresolved.
rows.evidence_quote: each well being tested approximately once every two months

rows.detail: Reservoir pressure is collected for modeling and operations and routinely updated, with FPP from step-rate tests; read at WAG headers and in new wells. Listed observation wells are not tied to monitoring.
rows.location: Injection zone, via WAG headers and new wells
rows.trigger_or_response: Unexplained pressure changes: investigate; reseal abandoned wells, manage lease-line fluids, or shut in injectors.
rows.evidence_quote: Measurements to determine FPP and reservoir pressure are routinely updated.

rows.detail: Routine field inspections of wells and surface facilities for white CO2 clouds, ice and fluid leaks; also used to spot unapproved drilling.
rows.trigger_or_response: Problem found: investigate, work order tracked to completion, leak quantified.
rows.evidence_quote: Field inspections are conducted on a routine basis by field personnel.

rows.detail: All field personnel wear H2S monitors (alarm at 10 ppm); injected gas is about 1% H2S, so H2S serves as a proxy for CO2 leaks.
rows.trigger_or_response: Alarm: protect personnel, investigate source, quantify CO2 leak for the annual report.
rows.evidence_quote: the H2S monitors, which are worn by all field personnel at all times, is used as a last method to detect leakage from wellbores.

rows.detail: Existing open- and cased-hole logs from 232 wells used to build the geomodel; no logging is run as monitoring.
rows.evidence_quote: These wells have digital open- or cased-hole logs that were used for correlation of formation tops.

rows.detail: Oxy participates in the public TexNet network and says it will keep monitoring for seismic signals; a one-time USGS review (M3.0+) found none in the field, nearest about 35 miles away. No site array.
rows.trigger_or_response: Seismic event: shut in nearby injectors (response plan).
rows.evidence_quote: will continue to monitor for seismic signals that could indicate the creation of potential leakage pathways in WSSAU

rows.detail: Past review of geologic and seismic evidence cited as showing no faults or fractures crossing the reservoir; no repeat seismic.
rows.evidence_quote: After reviewing geologic, seismic, operating, and other evidence, it has been concluded that there are no known faults or fractures

rows.detail: Subpart W emission factors and engineering estimates used to quantify surface equipment leaks and vents, reconciled with event-driven estimates to avoid double counting.
rows.evidence_quote: Oxy uses 40 CFR Part 98 Subpart W to estimate surface leaks from equipment at the WSSAU.

rows.detail: Pipeline leak detection: personnel monitor the field pipeline system continuously through SCADA.
rows.trigger_or_response: Leak detected: mitigate and quantify under Subpart W.
rows.evidence_quote: Personnel continuously monitor the pipeline system using the SCADA system and are able to detect and mitigate pipeline leaks expeditiously.

rows.detail: History-matched Eclipse reservoir model used to track injected CO2 and, through ongoing pattern modeling, to set injector targets; predictive modeling plus monitoring data to support the discontinuation request.
rows.evidence_quote: Track injected CO2, identify how and where CO2 is trapped in the WSSAU, and to monitor sequestration volumes and distribution.

notes: Same Oxy template as the Seminole San Andres Unit and South Plains plans. Producers are tested about every two months; the vocabulary has no bimonthly value, so frequency is periodic_unspecified. Two observation wells appear in the well count (p12) but the plan never says they are used for monitoring, so they are not coded as above-zone or reservoir-pressure monitoring. Existing cased-hole logs are mentioned only as geomodel inputs (coded mentioned_only). Table numbering is inconsistent (the well count is captioned Table 1 but cited as Table 2; the response plan is Table 2 but cited as Table 3). Figures are images.
